clue.text: Defence raised when things get too hot

definitions.text: Defence raised when things get too hot

parts.words: Defence raised when things get too hot
parts.note: a parasol is put up as a shield against strong sunlight, read as a military defence raised in a heated fight

explanation.surface: A fortification thrown up when a battle grows too fierce.
explanation.walkthrough: The words suggest siege warfare and things getting 'hot' in combat; the object is a sunny-day parasol held up overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning is literally a shield put up against the heat of the sun.

clue.text: In Cannes, a festival that's most reliable

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: At the French film festival, one event is the most dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: The most secure or trustworthy option is the one least likely to fail.

clue.text: Attila holds everything up in the ravine

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the built word from bottom to top
holds says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: Attila was king of the Huns, so he is a Hun
all means everything

explanation.surface: The warlord Attila halts all traffic in a mountain gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns HALLUN, Hun round all, into the answer reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a dry riverbed or gully is called by this name, so it is a ravine.

clue.text: Meat dish with wild oat as vegetable? That's controversial

parts.note: a Lancashire hotpot is a stew of meat under sliced potatoes

indicators.note: wild tells us to scramble the letters of oat

explanation.surface: A stew served with wild oats as its vegetable would cause argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes; the scrambled oat makes ATO, and 'as vegetable?' hints that the result names a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue too sensitive to handle, like something too hot to hold, is controversial.

clue.text: Not the gear you change in a 'car-the other one, Albert

definitions.text: Not the gear you change in a 'car-the other one, Albert

parts.words: Not the gear you change in a 'car-the other one, Albert
parts.note: the car part that lets the driving wheels turn at different speeds is a gear set the driver never shifts, and 'the other one' means a different one

explanation.surface: Someone tells Albert he has the wrong gear in mind: not the gearstick one.
explanation.walkthrough: The gear assembly on a car's axle is never changed by the driver, and 'the other one' gives a hint of 'different'.
explanation.definitionFit: The axle gearing that splits drive between the wheels is a car gear the driver never selects.

clue.text: Tea — ate when worried

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
fed means ate, as in 'the cattle fed'

explanation.surface: Someone eats their afternoon tea while anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rubbed raw or fretted by something is to be irritated and fretful, so the past tense fits worried.

clue.text: Accommodation top-hole if out of work, maybe

indicators.note: maybe says the remaining letters may be arranged another way
if out of says the letters for work are removed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Lodging that is first-rate if one is unemployed, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OP from TOPHOLE leaves THOLE, which 'maybe' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A place offering rooms to travellers provides accommodation.

clue.text: False story about ringleader causes bad feeling

indicators.note: about says the story goes around the other letter

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
the leader of 'ring' is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A lie told about the chief troublemaker stirs up resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people means conflict or ill will.

clue.text: Well-known bank elevated in USA by paltry numbers

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a famous sandbank in the North Sea
el is the American name for an elevated railway

explanation.surface: A famous bank, raised up in America, deals in small figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogger Bank, a North Sea shoal named in British shipping forecasts, is the bank; 'numbers' is the poetic word for verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial, badly made verse is poor poetry, and 'numbers' is an old word for metrical lines.

clue.text: Old castle put together in Shakespeare

definitions.text: Old castle put together in Shakespeare

parts.words: Old castle put together in Shakespeare
parts.note: joining the two words gives Oldcastle, the name Shakespeare first gave to his fat knight in Henry IV before renaming him

explanation.surface: An ancient fortress is assembled within the works of the Bard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Oldcastle was the original name of the fat knight in Henry IV; after protests from Oldcastle's descendants Shakespeare renamed him, so 'Old castle' run together points to the renamed character.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight Shakespeare first called Sir John Oldcastle is the same comic character under his later name.

clue.text: Pearls or horses, it's a bit of a racket

definitions.meaning: a strand of pearls threaded together
a stable's group of racehorses is called by the same word
one of the strung cords of a tennis racket

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a necklace strand, a trainer's group of racehorses and a gut cord in a tennis racket.

clue.text: D-day Phase One — though it did not use this platform

definitions.text: D-day Phase One — though it did not use this platform

parts.words: D-day Phase One — though it did not use this platform
parts.note: the first phase of the Normandy invasion was getting troops ashore, yet it used no pier, since troops waded from craft onto open beaches

explanation.surface: The first stage of the 1944 invasion, which made no use of a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phase of D-day was the coming ashore of troops; the platform for boats is a pier the troops did not use, as they landed on open beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty or floating pier where passengers and goods come ashore from boats is a platform.

clue.text: Military cover has arranged the decisive blow

indicators.note: arranged tells us to put the letters of 'has' into a new order

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the blow that ends a boxing match

explanation.surface: A piece of army headgear has set up the knockout punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall peaked cylindrical cap worn by soldiers is a military head covering.

clue.text: Oriental girl carried shoulder-high

definitions.note: the definition describes a thing worn on the shoulder, so read it as 'thing carried shoulder-high'

parts.note: E stands for East, so eastern or oriental
Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Eastern girl was hoisted onto someone's shoulders in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried shoulder-high' suggests a victor chaired by a crowd; here it describes the ornamental pad worn on the shoulder of a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornamental flap sits on the shoulder of a military coat, so it is literally borne at shoulder height.

clue.text: Many-coloured glass in the Tube? All done by mirrors

definitions.text: Many-coloured glass in the Tube? All done by mirrors

parts.words: Many-coloured glass in the Tube? All done by mirrors
parts.note: a toy tube holding bits of coloured glass whose patterns come from angled mirrors, dressed up as stained glass on the London Underground

explanation.surface: Coloured glass on the London Underground is a conjuring trick done with mirrors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tube' suggests the London Underground and 'all done by mirrors' a conjuror's patter; the tube is a toy holding loose coloured glass reflected by mirrors.
explanation.definitionFit: This optical toy is a tube with coloured fragments and mirrors that produce shifting symmetrical patterns.

clue.text: Rose turned Dobson into this kind of poet

annotationWithheld.why: Rose turned Dobson into this kind of poet: no parse found for SONNETEER; 'Rose turned' gives no run in the answer and the allusion to Dobson cannot be traced
annotationWithheld.clue: Rose turned Dobson into this kind of poet

clue.text: RAF's hard won goal, a girl for moulding

parts.note: the RAF motto Per ardua ad astra means through adversity to the stars, so its goal is the stars, astra in Latin
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: The air force won a hard-fought goal and a girl came for the sculpting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small convex bead round a column is an architectural moulding.

clue.text: Old boy starting court action, in the paper

parts.note: OB is a former pupil, an old boy
on a tennis court the player who serves starts the action

explanation.surface: A former pupil begins legal proceedings, as reported in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' suggests a lawsuit; it is tennis play begun by the one serving. The paper is the British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a long-running British Sunday newspaper.

clue.text: India, including Pakistan, being less than temperate?

parts.note: sub- is the prefix meaning under or below
continent means self-restrained or temperate

explanation.surface: A remark that the whole of India and Pakistan is less than moderate in its habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continent' here is the adjective meaning self-controlled, not a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: The large landmass of South Asia, India together with Pakistan, is a region slightly smaller than a full continent.

clue.text: An arid sort of pope

indicators.note: sort of suggests a version of the letters of 'an arid'

explanation.surface: A rather dry kind of pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Several popes took this name, including Hadrian IV, the only English one.

clue.text: Inferno as Shelley's work

parts.note: hell is the inferno
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hellish blaze is how Shelley's writing is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley wrote a lyrical drama of this title, the Greek name for Greece.

clue.text: Those controlling the roasts perhaps in an electric oven

definitions.text: Those controlling the roasts perhaps in an electric oven

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of 'the roasts' might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: The devices regulating the joints of meat in an electric cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: Variable resistors set the current, and so the heat, in an electric oven, which controls the roasting; 'perhaps' rearranges THE ROASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable resistors regulate electric current, as in the temperature controls of an electric cooker.

clue.text: 2" Blest pair of s Voice and Verse ' (Milton)

definitions.text: Blest pair of s Voice and Verse

parts.words: Blest pair of s Voice and Verse
parts.note: Milton's ode At a Solemn Music opens by calling Voice and Verse a blest pair of sea nymphs who sing, so the blank wants that word

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's 'At a Solemn Music' begins 'Blest pair of Sirens, pledges of Heaven's joy, ... Voice and Verse'; the blank takes the singular with the printed s.
explanation.definitionFit: The singing sea nymphs of Greek myth lured sailors, and Milton names voice and verse as two of them.

clue.text: Furnish in French style, owing to the finish

indicators.note: to the finish places the word for owing at the end of the answer

parts.note: en is the French word for in
due means owing, as in money due

explanation.surface: Fitting out a room in a French manner because the decoration is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow or invest someone with a quality is to supply or furnish them with it.

clue.text: Control Earth's gravity over the Pole

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to Earth's gravity
taken as written
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: Earth's gravitational pull is in charge above the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule or direct is to control.

clue.text: Would this witness be a man of the cloth

definitions.text: Would this witness be a man of the cloth

parts.words: Would this witness be a man of the cloth
parts.note: a key witness in law has a name that also means cloth, so the clue asks whether such a witness is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A question whether a certain court witness would be a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'man of the cloth' is a priest; the joke is that the legal term for an important witness uses a word that also means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric or cloth is called this, and in law a witness whose evidence matters is a witness of this kind.

clue.text: Source of talk of a wild cat round Central Park

indicators.note: round says the wild cat goes around the other piece

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of park

explanation.surface: Gossip about a wild animal prowling through Central Park in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat houses the vocal cords, so speech comes from it.

clue.text: Fishes a Banbury lady has on hand down

parts.note: the fine lady of the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock horse to Banbury Cross' is referred to as her
the rhyme says she has rings on her fingers

explanation.surface: A fine lady from Banbury goes fishing with jewellery on.
explanation.walkthrough: The British nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock horse to Banbury Cross' has a fine lady with 'rings on her fingers and bells on her toes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvery sea fish caught in shoals, the plural matching 'fishes'.
